issues.body: The round-one concern remains through the public compatibility projection. equality_join_security() returns authenticated_abort(), whose adversary is SemiHonest, but the test requires auth.malicious_security(0) == HonestMajorityAbort and then asserts is_malicious_secure(). Public docs likewise advertise that projection. A consumer using the existing malicious_security API therefore sees this experimental, externally unaudited path as malicious-secure despite the AXIS-1 caveat and pending sq-qhy4 gate. Moving the claim between descriptor axes does not contain it when the supported public projection reconstructs the prohibited claim.
issues.fix_hint: Until sq-qhy4 closes, make the public projection for this descriptor return SemiHonestOnly (or introduce an explicitly experimental/tamper-evidence status that malicious_security/is_malicious_secure cannot interpret as malicious security). Update the test to assert that no public API classifies the path as malicious-secure, while separately testing the experimental abort/tamper-evidence property. Keep the current caveats and experimental names.
issues.title: Legacy security projection still publicly classifies the unaudited path as malicious-secure

verdict.summary: Round 2 removes the fixed row-count/wall-clock claim and adds prominent experimental/unaudited caveats, so it is improving. However, the prior major issue is not fully contained: although the new descriptor sets AXIS-1 to SemiHonest, its public legacy projection still returns HonestMajorityAbort and is_malicious_secure() == true. Thus callers using the advertised malicious_security API still receive a positive malicious-security classification before sq-qhy4 external review. The new guard test actually pins this contradictory state rather than preventing it.
